name: Show a teacher's record beside the results of the classes they teach, for appraisal and deployment
priorityReason: Reads data the other use cases produce and creates none of its own. It cannot be built before they exist.

goal.capability: to see each teacher's attendance and appraisal record beside the results of the classes they teach
goal.outcome: appraisal, deployment and training decisions rest on figures set side by side rather than on impressions

secondaryActors.involvement: Reviews it by department, class or individual, and uses it in appraisal.
Sees it for the subjects and sections they oversee.
Is the subject of the record and sees their own figures only.

preconditions.condition: Staff records exist with their assignments for the session.
Results have been approved for the exams being read. Unapproved results are not included (BR-3).
Teachers are matched to classes, sections and subjects through the timetable for the session.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Principal, School Admin, Coordinator or Teacher.

postConditions: Each teacher's attendance, appraisal and result figures are presented side by side for the period chosen.
Each teacher was matched to the classes, sections and subjects assigned to them for the session, so a figure belongs to the person who taught it.
Only approved results were included, since an unapproved result is not yet the school's view of anything.

The reader saw what their role permits — the Principal across the school and its campuses, the School Admin by department, the Coordinator for what they oversee, and a teacher their own figures alone.
Nothing was written. The comparison reads the records and produces no rating, no ranking and no score of its own.
The comparison is available as a report for the Principal.
A teacher who took a class part way through the session is shown against the period they actually taught it, not the whole year.

dataFields.name: Period
dataFields.validation: The period being compared — a term, a session, or a date range.

dataFields.name: Attendance
dataFields.validation: The teacher's own attendance for the period, from the staff attendance record (BR-2).

dataFields.name: Leave taken
dataFields.validation: Paid and unpaid leave taken in the period.

dataFields.name: Class average
dataFields.validation: The average result of the sections they taught, from approved results only (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Pass rate
dataFields.validation: The proportion of their students who passed.

dataFields.name: Appraisal
dataFields.validation: The appraisal record where one exists. Appraisals are not in MVP, so this is often empty (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Taught from and to
dataFields.validation: The period the teacher actually held the section, so a part-session assignment is not judged over the whole year (BR-6).

businessRules.rule: Each teacher is matched to the classes, sections and subjects assigned to them for the session, so a result figure belongs to the person who actually taught it.
Attendance, appraisal and result figures are presented side by side. The comparison is the point; a result figure alone says nothing about the teaching behind it.
Only approved results are included. An unapproved result is not yet the school's view of anything, and a comparison built on one would move when it was released.
The reader filters by department, class, subject, branch or period. A single figure for a session hides a term in which something changed.

What a reader sees follows their role. The Principal sees the school and its campuses, the School Admin their branch by department, the Coordinator their own subjects and sections, and a teacher their own figures alone.
A teacher who took a section part way through the session is shown against the period they actually taught it. Judging somebody on a result from before they arrived is not a comparison.
The comparison writes nothing. It produces no rating, no ranking and no score of its own, and changes no record it reads.
An appraisal figure appears where an appraisal record exists. Formal appraisals are not in MVP, so the column is often empty and is shown as not recorded rather than as a low score.
Leadership uses the comparison in appraisal, deployment and training decisions. It supports a judgement; it does not make one.
A result figure is always shown with the number of students behind it. An average over six students is not comparable with one over sixty.
Running the comparison is recorded, since it concerns named individuals and is used in decisions about them.

basicFlow.userAction: Chooses the scope and the period to compare over.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the teachers in scope for that period.
Matches each teacher to the classes, sections and subjects assigned to them for the session, with the period each was actually held.
Reads each teacher's own attendance and leave for the period.
Reads the approved results of the sections they taught, and excludes any result not yet released.
Presents attendance, appraisal and result figures side by side, with the number of students behind each result, and shows only what the reader's role permits.

basicFlow.userAction: Filters by department, class, subject, branch or period.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Narrows the comparison without widening what the reader may see.

basicFlow.userAction: Produces the comparison as a report.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Produces the report, having written nothing and rated nobody.

alternateFlows.condition: An exam's results have not been approved
alternateFlows.behaviour: That exam is excluded, since a comparison built on an unreleased result would move when it was released (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: A teacher took the section part way through the session
alternateFlows.behaviour: They are shown against the period they actually taught it, not the whole year (BR-6).
They see the subjects and sections they oversee and nothing beyond them (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: A teacher opens their own figures
alternateFlows.behaviour: They see their own attendance and their own classes' results, and no colleague's (BR-5).
The column reads not recorded rather than showing a low score, since appraisals are not in MVP (BR-8).
The comparison runs across branches, giving the group picture rather than one campus (BR-5).

exceptions.condition: No approved result exists for the period
exceptions.systemResponse: The result columns are empty and say so, rather than showing zero (BR-3).
exceptions.messageShown: No approved results for this period. Attendance and appraisal are shown alone.

exceptions.condition: A teacher has no assignment for the session
exceptions.systemResponse: They do not appear in the comparison, since there is nothing to compare them against.

exceptions.condition: A section has very few students
exceptions.systemResponse: The result is shown with the student count beside it rather than as a bare average (BR-10).

exceptions.condition: A Coordinator filters to a department they do not oversee
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

exceptions.condition: A teacher attempts to see a colleague's figures
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

exceptions.condition: A user looks for a rating or a rank produced by the comparison
exceptions.systemResponse: There is none. It presents figures and makes no judgement (BR-7).

exceptions.condition: The timetable for the session is not published
exceptions.systemResponse: Teachers cannot be matched to sections and the comparison cannot run (BR-1).
exceptions.messageShown: The timetable for this session is not published. Teachers cannot be matched to their classes.

departures.requirement: The comparison writes nothing to any record it reads, and produces no rating, ranking or score of its own.
An unapproved result never appears, so a figure quoted in an appraisal cannot move afterwards.
A result is attributed only for the period the teacher actually held the section, so nobody is judged on a result from before they arrived.
A result average is never shown without the number of students behind it.
Every run is recorded with who ran it and over what scope, because it concerns named individuals and is used in decisions about them.
The comparison holds no data of its own and is produced on demand from the records it reads.

openQuestions.question: Appraisal figures are a stated input, but formal appraisals are not in MVP. What fills that column at launch?
Is a teacher shown their own comparison, and should they see how they sit against a department average?
openQuestions.assumption: Their own figures only as modelled. The department average is not shown to them.

openQuestions.question: Should the comparison account for the intake of a section, so a teacher of a weaker group is not judged against a stronger one?
openQuestions.assumption: Not modelled, and it is the commonest objection to this kind of comparison.

openQuestions.question: What period is the natural unit — a term, a session, or a rolling year?
May a teacher challenge a figure used in their appraisal, and through what route?

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
